discovery: Squeezed states of light and their use to surpass the standard quantum limit in precision measurement
motivation: In 1981 Caves showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations entering an interferometer's dark port set its sensitivity limit, and that injecting squeezed vacuum could beat this 'standard quantum limit'. Kimble's group then generated strongly squeezed light with optical parametric oscillators (1986) and demonstrated sub-shot-noise interferometry, turning squeezing from a theoretical curiosity into a laboratory tool. Schnabel developed high-purity squeezed-light sources at gravitational-wave frequencies, achieving record squeezing levels and the first sustained use in an observatory, GEO600 (2011). Squeezed light is now operating in Advanced LIGO and Virgo, raising the rate of detected black-hole and neutron-star mergers by tens of percent, and underpins quantum-enhanced sensing more broadly. This is a rare case in which a deep insight into quantum measurement became an instrument that expands what humanity can observe of the universe.
